html:
SMTO-CMP-0009 — A tool's own finish check isn't satisfied yet

GUID: 4c5a028a-8bda-4740-8672-9943ff25c6d1
Slug: completion-capability-verifier-unmet
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • A tool used in this task has its own rule for when its work counts as done, and the saved result doesn't meet that rule yet. SMTO kept the work done so far.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Technical details in this panel to see which tool's check failed and what it expected. The tool reports the exact condition that's missing, so you know what to look at.
  2. Check the result that tool was meant to produce, for example in the system or service it works with. The work may be finished but not yet confirmed, or it may still need a step.
  3. Select Resume, or describe what's done and what's left in the "Continue this conversation" box under the task, then select Continue. SMTO keeps finished work, so it can address only the unmet check.
  4. Don't select Restart task while you're unsure what the tool already did. Restart begins a fresh attempt and doesn't undo earlier actions, so the tool's work could happen twice.

What success looks like

  • The task shows Completed and this check no longer appears.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, naming the tool if you know it. Check whether the earlier action already happened before anything is repeated. Don't restart the task; that could repeat the tool's actions.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A capability's registered verify_completion hook returned unmet requirements for a cited receipt (reason capability_verifier_unmet), so completion was rejected.

What this means

  • A registered capability completion verifier returns unmet requirements for a cited receipt. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • A registered capability completion verifier returns unmet requirements for a cited receipt.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the verifier's exact requirement and the retained receipt fields.

How to fix it

  • Read the unmet requirement list in the run's completion.rejected event together with the cited receipt's fields; the hook is the capability's verify_completion, collected by completion_verifiers in src/agent_runtime/native/completion.py. Satisfy the requirement with a current observation in this run, or correct the capability's verifier if its rule is wrong; do not replay the operation just to re-trigger the check.
  • Inspect the named capability verification requirement and satisfy it using authoritative observations.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported authoritative observation satisfies the named capability verification condition.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
